title: Volume 1 Chapter 4: Candy Coating & Brush Painting 2
content: "Hello! Azuma-kun, I’m here!"
"Ah!"
I jumped at the call from outside the garage.
"Can I come in?"
Usually, she barged in without waiting for a reply.
Maybe she was being more polite today because she had a friend with her.
Thinking that, I hurriedly put away the model into the box and tidied up the workbench.
"Uh, yeah, come in..."
I tried to keep my composure and replied to Sayori.
—I didn’t want her to know that I was making models to distract myself because I couldn’t stay calm around her.
As Sayori entered the garage, another girl followed her in.
She lightly bowed her head in greeting.
"Hello, I’m Karla Shiba. Please call me Karla."
Sayori's friend, Karla.
The first thing that caught my eye was her strikingly blue skin, which made it clear she was a demi-human at first glance.
"Ah, um, nice to meet you, I’m Hajime Azuma."
"So you’re the rumored nail artist. I’m so happy to meet you; Sayori always brags about you."
"Is that so?"
"Yeah! Because Azuma-kun is amazing!"
Sayori puffed out her chest proudly.
Being praised like that was undeniably embarrassing.
"Um... Shiba-san is a demi-human, right?"
"Ah, just call me Karla. I’m not a fan of formalities. Let’s keep it casual."
She said something similar to Sayori. Is that how all gals are?
Karla Shiba was dressed in casual gal clothing. She wore a thick hooded parka, but the parka had four sleeves sewn into it.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/6iXyqpg.jpeg

The two arms near her back were supporting her head from behind the parka. Of the two arms in front, the left hand was shoved into a pocket while the other held a lollipop. She wore a short skirt with leggings underneath. Compared to Sayori, who exposed more skin, Karla gave off a somewhat shadowy vibe, even though they were both dragon girls. Were they of the same kind? Well, it’s not like being fellow introverts meant they would get along.
“Sorry, but eating and drinking isn’t allowed in this garage.”
“Oh, my bad!”
As I pointed it out, Karla immediately crunched down on the candy and swallowed it. For a brief moment, her tongue, like any normal human’s, was visible and red.
“I’m a demi-human with blood from a god-like being through the continent… So, I might look a bit surprising, but let’s be friends!”
“A god, huh… Are there really demi-humans like that?”
The demi-humans I knew were mostly humans with animal traits, so the idea of a god-like being felt quite fantastical.
“Well, if you trace my family tree back, it kind of leads to that, but whether or not gods actually exist is another story, right? It could be a lie.”
Karla chuckled. Compared to Sayori, her demeanor was much more laid-back, straying from the typical image of a fashion model.
“Besides, dragons are pretty mythical creatures themselves.”
“No, no, I’m living and breathing right here!”
Sayori pointed to herself, asserting her existence. Well, it was indeed a tough call between believing in dragons or gods. Regardless, it was clear that she was a demi-human with different blood.
“But you really do your nails in a garage. Oh, and you have a lot of plastic models!”
“I’m just borrowing them from my dad. This is originally a workspace for models.”
“Hehe. Sorry for barging into your precious space with two girls!”
Karla joked, scratching her head with her back arms. With four arms, her subtle gestures were entirely different from a human’s.
“Karla isn’t just a reader model like me; she’s a professional model affiliated with an agency!”
“Wait, really?”
Honestly, I didn’t quite understand what being a professional model entailed.
“So… um, a celebrity?”
“Ahaha. It’s not that big of a deal. I don’t get many jobs, and my agency scolds me to focus on school.”
“School… you’re not going?”
“I’ve been skipping classes under the pretense of work, and my grades have dropped… They keep telling me to study properly.”
Karla sighed heavily. It seemed that professionals had their own troubles.
“But Karla, you’re always popular with readers!”
“Is that so? How so…?”
She seemed to have a strong visual personality, but perhaps that was what appealed to people.
“Ah, it’s with other demi-human girls, you see. My fans have been increasing. Since I look different from the norm, it seems like girls like me doing modeling inspires them.”
“Wow.”
Though she spoke with a lack of enthusiasm, I could catch a glimpse of her pride as a professional.
“Well, I’m technically marketed as a charismatic gal model.”
Karla struck a pose, twisting her waist and extending her four arms in all directions. I didn’t really get it, but seeing Sayori clap innocently made me think it must be a professional pose.
“...But it’s really you doing my nails, right?”
“Ah, yeah. Of course.”
That was the plan, but…
“Just remember, I’m an amateur. I can’t guarantee the quality that would satisfy a professional model.”
“Oh, come on! I saw the photos Sayori sent. They were super pretty and without any unevenness! I can’t do it this well myself!”
Karla spread her four arms wide, showing off her total of twenty nails.
“Besides, I have double the nails of a regular person. A good nail artist is something I desperately want!”
“Karla, what are you going to do with more hands than that?”
Sayori laughed heartily. Karla stuck her tongue out playfully. They seemed to be in perfect sync, being friends.
“Well, if you say so, I’ll do it.”
“Yay! Looking forward to it, big brother♪”
Karla, who had been acting lethargic, finally showed a smile and winked at me.
I tilted my head, not understanding why she was being so friendly.
“Well, whatever. Just show me your nails.”
I sat down at the work desk and gestured for Karla to sit across from me.
“—Hey, Sayori, is this big brother kind of a stiff?”
“Yeah, pretty much.”
“Seriously? I gave him my best wink!”
“...What are you two talking about?”
I couldn’t grasp their conversation. My mind was already filled with thoughts on how to paint Karla’s nails, leaving little room for engaging in their chatter.
“Nothing at all! Well then, let’s get started~”
Karla returned to her lethargic expression and extended her blue-skinned hand toward me.
Karla sat across the work desk. Sayori perched herself on the couch behind her, where she had sat while getting her pedicure, seemingly waiting for her turn.

First, I carefully observed Karla’s hands. Her skin was a deep blue, and her nails were a darker shade, almost black. At first glance, it might seem unhealthy, but for a demi-human like Karla, this was likely a healthy color.
If I didn’t properly form the polish layer, the color of her nails might show through, which I wanted to avoid. I needed to be meticulous with the base treatment.
“How have you been doing your nails until now?”
“Oh, well, at a nail salon with a familiar nail artist… The polish tends to peel off, but I had the nail artist do the surface treatment somehow. Like, they would file it with a metal file.”
“Sounds almost the same as Sayori…”
“She was a great nail artist, but she retired. I’m really glad to have you take over!”
I lightly touched Karla’s nails. I didn’t feel the rough pain like I did with Sayori’s nails. However, I sensed a metallic hardness from her touch. (It feels like a hard plastic…)
There’s no way her nails are actually made of plastic, but they seemed to hold more mysteries than Sayori’s.
“For now, let’s try grinding them down.”
“Oh, you’re bringing out some serious tools!”

Karla giggled, impressed. Sayori cheered me on seriously, while Karla seemed to take a more laid-back approach. It wasn’t unpleasant, but it made me realize how precious Sayori’s straightforward compliments were.

I began to grind down Karla’s nails. The shavings appeared immediately. They were black shavings, the same color as her nails, making it easy to tell. What material are Karla’s nails made of? (Black… maybe carbon material? No way, right?)
There was no point in pondering it, so I decided to focus on grinding.
“Let me know if it hurts.”
“Oh, I’m fine! You’re pretty skilled with your hands, big brother.”
“Not really.”
“No, no, you’re being modest. Sayori and I are the epitome of clumsiness, so I envy you. Just the other day, Sayori—”
“Wait! Karla! Don’t say unnecessary things!”
“Oh, I got scolded.”
Karla giggled mischievously. As long as they were talking to each other, I didn’t have to join in, which was a relief. Conversations during work could be quite taxing.
But—(She has… a lot of fingers.)

I had known that from the start with her four arms, but the number was indeed overwhelming. Karla’s arms seemed to branch from her shoulder joints, allowing both the front and back arms to move freely. With two on each side, I found myself forgetting which hand I was working with. I had to be careful.
“Ah, sorry, is this hard to do after all?”
Karla asked, sensing my tension.
“No, it’s not that… but it is quite a lot. As an amateur, it might take me some time.”
“As long as you do it carefully, that’s fine!”
“I’ll try my best—but still, you’ve been relying on a pro until now, so wouldn’t it have been better to stick with a professional nail artist?”
“Well, that’s…”
Karla glanced at Sayori with a somewhat troubled expression.
“I wanted to see what kind of person the nail artist Sayori always brags about is like.”
“Bragging… is that what I’m doing?”
“Lately, it’s been amazing, right? You’re well-loved♪”
It felt a bit different from love.
“Well, I can’t change the fact that I have four arms, so please get used to it.”
“Ah, sorry for making you feel awkward…”
No one likes to have their body commented on.
“No, it’s fine. There’s nothing I can do about being different. Plus, this body isn’t so bad, you know?”
“I can do things like this, see?”
Karla, leaving her left hand in place, extended her right arm from behind and reached out to touch my head, patting it.
“Good job, big brother! You’re doing great!”
“W-What are you doing?!”
Before I could raise my voice, Sayori stood up.
“What do you mean, I’m thanking him for doing my nails!”
“Azuma-kun is uncomfortable! Stop it!”
For some reason, Sayori was speaking on my behalf. I hadn’t said anything, though—
“Oops. I got scolded.”
“Hands off, okay!”
Sayori confronted Karla. Why was Sayori the one making the rules?
“...It’s dangerous to touch too much while working, especially since I’m holding tools right now.”
I decided to give a warning as well. Whether Karla understood or not, she just replied with a lethargic “Okay.”
While we were having that conversation, the nail grinding process came to an end. Up to this point, everything had gone smoothly without any issues.
(Good, let’s move on to the base coat.)

I quickly applied the base coat. I started with the first right hand, then the second right hand, followed by the first left hand, and finally the second left hand. Since there were twenty fingers, by the time I finished painting them all, the first nails I painted would be nicely dried. After that, I would move on to the base color.
(So many… so many…)

It was just a repetitive task of applying paint. In Karla’s case, I had to apply double the amount, so maintaining concentration was key. She was a professional model; I couldn’t afford to make any mistakes.
Naturally, my words became fewer.
(Alright, just do it the same way.)
The base color was a dark purple. This was to create the image of “stars floating in the night sky,” as requested by Sayori, representing the darkness of the night with a dark hue.
I focused on applying the base coat to all twenty nails without losing concentration.
“Phew.”
Once the task reached a pause, I finally exhaled.
“Wow, as expected of Sayori’s favorite! You paint beautifully!”
Karla looked at her four hands, nodding in satisfaction.
“We’re not done yet.”

Despite her tone suggesting we were finished, this was just the beginning of the nail job. Just like candy coating, I would apply a clear color on top to express depth and gloss, adding a twinkling effect like stars.
(First, let’s prepare a dish.)
In model-making, it’s common to mix several paints. I took out a metal paint dish and poured in the clear color.
(As for the amount—well, since Karla has a lot of nails, I’ll pour a bit more.)

A thick, transparent top coat was poured into the dish. The distinct smell of nail polish, stemming from the thinner, spread through the air. Since it was a highly volatile paint, the scent spread quickly.
(Let’s mix in the glitter powder…)
I added the gold glitter powder Sayori had given me. Since I wanted to create a starry sky effect, it was ideal for the glitter to be sparse.
Using a nail spatula, I quickly mixed the paint and powder. The trick here was to press the paint down while mixing to avoid incorporating air.
“It’s like you’re cooking, Azuma-kun.”
“It’s nail art, not cooking.”

I received a comment from someone who clearly had never cooked before. I pulled out a detail brush used for models. Since I had mixed glitter into the paint, I couldn’t use the brush that came with the small bottle.
With a detail brush, I could manage fine work, and I was also familiar with it. Now, all that was left was to paint.
“Alright, put your hand out.”
“Okay, okay.”
“This is the last step, so be careful.”
I had been nervous at the start, but it seemed like I would be able to finish smoothly. There hadn’t been any major mistakes.
If I finished with the brush I was used to, I was sure they would be pleased.
—That’s what I thought, but I was underestimating the situation.
As I painted the glittery top coat over the dark purple, the sparkle shimmered against the deep color reminiscent of the night sky. For now, I could say I had fulfilled the client’s request.
Both Karla and Sayori exclaimed in awe simultaneously.
While it was nice that they were pleased, I was actually feeling anxious.
Because—(The top coat I poured into the dish… it dries quickly…!)
The moment it was exposed to air, the top coat began to dry and thicken.
This was bad.
If I applied the high-viscosity top coat as it was, the paint layer wouldn’t be uniform. As a result, it could become uneven or create strange bumps, ultimately affecting the finish.
(Ah, nail polish dries quickly! I completely forgot…)
I had been treating it just like model paint.
Considering the number of nails Karla had, I had poured quite a bit of top coat into the dish. If I continued like this, I wouldn’t be able to use all the paint.
Now I understood why nail polish came in such small glass bottles.
When applying nail polish, it was to minimize the surface area exposed to air to prevent evaporation, not just because it was cute.
Model paint doesn’t dry this quickly because it involves a lot of mixing and stirring. Even with careful work, there’s enough time to manage it—
But nail polish is different.
If I poured out so much at once, it would affect the finish.
(What should I do? Use thinner… but that would change the ratio with the powder, right?)
The polish that had dried and hardened could be softened by adding a few drops of remover.
But even then, it would likely change the finish significantly.
If I thinned the hardened polish and painted it, then thinned it again—repeating this would alter the ratio with the glitter powder.
As I painted Karla’s twenty nails, the finish could end up looking completely different from the first to the last.
The paint already on the brush was beginning to harden as well. If I continued using it, it might create unevenness.
(…Well)
To be honest,
Even if there were a few uneven spots or if the finish was a bit sloppy, people who don’t care won’t mind.
It’s the same with model-making. Some modelers are fine with a slightly rough finish as long as it’s completed, while others obsess over the details and waste time and effort.
If it’s a hobby, it’s perfectly fine to finish it however you see fit.
But.
(I’m doing this because they asked me to.)
Sayori and Karla. Both genuinely wanted to enjoy their nails.
That’s why they asked me.
Moreover, this was for a photoshoot. Sayori and Karla would be going into the shoot as part of their work. Yet, I couldn’t allow a compromise in the nails just because I found it troublesome.
I was fully aware of my inexperience and the technical gaps I had. But still, I wanted to do everything I could here. I had to.
“Sorry, I’m going to change my approach a bit.”
“Oh, is that okay? What about that dish?”
“Yeah.”
I decided not to use the paint I had already made.
First, I prepared a new paint dish. Then I switched brushes.
While the detail brush was good for fine work, it wasn’t suitable for quickly painting larger areas. I took out a flat brush that I hadn’t used much.
This one would likely feel similar to the brush that came with the nail polish.
“Um… did the atmosphere change a bit?”
“Maybe he’s concentrating.”
Sayori and Karla whispered to each other.
I could hear their words, but I couldn’t respond as I focused on my work.
(I can’t pour out a large amount of paint at once. Just a little at a time.)
I poured enough top coat for one to two nails into the paint dish.
Then I mixed in the glitter powder as well, maintaining the same ratio as before. I added about half of it by eye and mixed it with the spatula.
(I have to use it all before it dries, and take out more as needed. I have no choice but to balance speed and accuracy.)
In a situation where speed was also required, the challenge was how accurately I could create and apply the paint.
(—Now!)
I swiftly painted the broad areas of the nails with the flat brush.
This was a one-shot deal; there was no room for corrections. After applying the top coat in the center, I quickly painted the uncoated areas on both sides.
(Good, the flat brush is definitely a better fit.)
The detail brush wasn’t bad, but the flat brush was more suitable for painting nails.
I wondered if there were brushes specifically for nail polish. I should look it up next time.
(I’m usually clumsy, but—please, today, just work for me.)
I told my fingertips.
